review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

5:1.sourceText: Καὶ εἶδον ἐπὶ τὴν δεξιὰν τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου βιβλίον γεγραμμένον ἔσωθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν, κατεσφραγισμένον σφραγῖσιν ἑπτά.
5:1.targetText: Then I saw a scroll in the right hand of the One seated on the throne. It had writing on both sides and was sealed with seven seals.

groups.note: The article with the participle καθημένου ("the one seated") is rendered of the One seated.
The participle γεγραμμένον ("written") is rendered had writing.
ἔσωθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν ("inside and on the back") is rendered on both sides.
The dative σφραγῖσιν supplies with.

unmappedTarget.reason: English starts a new sentence and supplies a subject for the participle γεγραμμένον.
English joins the two participles; the Greek has no καί here.

5:2.sourceText: καὶ εἶδον ἄγγελον ἰσχυρὸν κηρύσσοντα ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ Τίς ἄξιος ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ λῦσαι τὰς σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ;
5:2.targetText: And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming in a loud voice, “Who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the possessive αὐτοῦ ("its") unexpressed and writes the seals.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek has none.

5:3.sourceText: καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ οὐδὲ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς οὐδὲ ὑποκάτω τῆς γῆς ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον οὔτε βλέπειν αὐτό.
5:3.targetText: But no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or look inside it.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:4.sourceText: καὶ ἔκλαιον πολὺ, ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἄξιος εὑρέθη ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον οὔτε βλέπειν αὐτό.
5:4.targetText: And I began to weep bitterly, because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or look inside it.

groups.note: I renders the person of ἔκλαιον; BSB follows a reading with an extra word here.

5:5.sourceText: καὶ εἷς ἐκ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων λέγει μοι Μὴ κλαῖε· ἰδοὺ ἐνίκησεν ὁ Λέων ὁ ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς Ἰούδα, ἡ Ῥίζα Δαυείδ, ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ τὰς ἑπτὰ σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ.
5:5.targetText: Then one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep! Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed to open the scroll and its seven seals.”

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated article before ἐκ ("the one from") has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:6.sourceText: Καὶ εἶδον ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων Ἀρνίον ἑστηκὸς ὡς ἐσφαγμένον, ἔχων κέρατα ἑπτὰ καὶ ὀφθαλμοὺς ἑπτά, οἵ εἰσιν τὰ ἑπτὰ Πνεύματα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀπεσταλμένοι εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν.
5:6.targetText: Then I saw a Lamb who appeared to have been slain, standing in the center of the throne, encircled by the four living creatures and the elders. The Lamb had seven horns and seven eyes, which represent the seven Spirits of God sent out into all the earth.

groups.note: The second ἐν μέσῳ ("in the midst of") is rendered encircled by, which BSB applies to both the living creatures and the elders.
ὡς ("as though") is rendered appeared.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB restructures the phrase, so the καί joining the throne and the living creatures has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English starts a new sentence and supplies the subject of the participle ἔχων.

5:7.sourceText: καὶ ἦλθεν καὶ εἴληφεν ἐκ τῆς δεξιᾶς τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου.
5:7.targetText: And He came and took the scroll from the right hand of the One seated on the throne.

groups.note: The article with the participle καθημένου ("the one seated") is rendered of the One seated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of took; the Greek has none.

5:8.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἔλαβεν τὸ βιβλίον, τὰ τέσσερα ζῷα καὶ οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες πρεσβύτεροι ἔπεσαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Ἀρνίου, ἔχοντες ἕκαστος κιθάραν καὶ φιάλας χρυσᾶς γεμούσας θυμιαμάτων, αἵ εἰσιν αἱ προσευχαὶ τῶν ἁγίων.
5:8.targetText: When He had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb. Each one had a harp, and they were holding golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.

groups.note: Same number, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The participle ἔχοντες governs both objects; BSB renders it again as were holding.

unmappedSource.reason: This opening καί only links to the previous verse; BSB starts the sentence with When.

unmappedTarget.reason: A participle has no person; English supplies the subject.

5:9.sourceText: καὶ ᾄδουσιν ᾠδὴν καινὴν λέγοντες Ἄξιος εἶ λαβεῖν τὸ βιβλίον καὶ ἀνοῖξαι τὰς σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐσφάγης καὶ ἠγόρασας τῷ Θεῷ ἐν τῷ αἵματί σου ἐκ πάσης φυλῆς καὶ γλώσσης καὶ λαοῦ καὶ ἔθνους,
5:9.targetText: And they sang a new song:  “Worthy are You to take the scroll and open its seals, because You were slain, and by Your blood You purchased for God those from every tribe and tongue and people and nation.

groups.note: The dative Θεῷ supplies for.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB introduces the song with a colon, so λέγοντες ("saying") has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for purchased; the Greek has none here.

5:10.sourceText: καὶ ἐποίησας αὐτοὺς τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν βασιλείαν καὶ ἱερεῖς, καὶ βασιλεύσουσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
5:10.targetText: You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will reign upon the earth.”

groups.note: The dative Θεῷ supplies to.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence, so καί has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies to be with the second object of ἐποίησας; the Greek has no verb here.
BSB adds serve to bring out the dative τῷ Θεῷ ("to God").

5:11.sourceText: καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἀγγέλων πολλῶν κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ τῶν ζῴων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, καὶ ἦν ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτῶν μυριάδες μυριάδων καὶ χιλιάδες χιλιάδων,
5:11.targetText: Then I looked, and I heard the voices of many angels and living creatures and elders encircling the throne, and their number was myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The article has no distinct counterpart; the possessive αὐτῶν is rendered their.

5:12.sourceText: λέγοντες φωνῇ μεγάλῃ Ἄξιός ἐστιν τὸ Ἀρνίον τὸ ἐσφαγμένον λαβεῖν τὴν δύναμιν καὶ πλοῦτον καὶ σοφίαν καὶ ἰσχὺν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ δόξαν καὶ εὐλογίαν.
5:12.targetText: In a loud voice they were saying:  “Worthy is the Lamb, who was slain, to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing!”

groups.note: The dative φωνῇ supplies In.
BSB's Greek text has another form of this adjective with the same meaning.
The article with the participle ἐσφαγμένον is rendered who was slain.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: A participle has no person; English supplies the subject.

5:13.sourceText: καὶ πᾶν κτίσμα ὃ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ὑποκάτω τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης ἐστίν, καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς πάντα, ἤκουσα λέγοντας Τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ καὶ τῷ Ἀρνίῳ ἡ εὐλογία καὶ ἡ τιμὴ καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
5:13.targetText: And I heard every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and in the sea, and all that is in them, saying:  “To Him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be praise and honor and glory and power forever and ever!”

groups.note: The article τὰ ("the things") with ἐν αὐτοῖς is rendered that … in them.
The article with the participle καθημένῳ is rendered To Him who sits.
The dative Ἀρνίῳ supplies to.
The genitive τῶν αἰώνων ("of the ages") completes the idiom forever and ever; there is no separate Greek and.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the relative clause ὃ … ἐστίν ("which is") without English words.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:14.sourceText: καὶ τὰ τέσσερα ζῷα ἔλεγον Ἀμήν, καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἔπεσαν καὶ προσεκύνησαν.
5:14.targetText: And the four living creatures said, “Amen,” and the elders fell down and worshiped.

groups.note: Same number, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
